facts.fact: 她回到邻居的客厅；和她先前猜的一样，这里现在和刚才那间卧室一样破败
facts.anchor: I was back in my neighbour’s living room. As I’d suspected earlier, it was now as dilapidated as the bedroom before.

facts.fact: 沙发垫塌陷、裂开，泡沫从角上冒出来
facts.anchor: The sofa cushions were sunken and ripped, their foam spilling out at the corners.

facts.fact: 壁炉在崩裂、发潮；咖啡桌上蒙着一层污垢和老鼠屎
facts.anchor: The fireplace was crumbling and damp. The coffee table was covered in a layer of grime and mouse droppings

facts.fact: 她闪过一个念头：那些发苦的绿色玻璃碎片，在她试着吞下去时割开她的喉咙
facts.anchor: I briefly imagined those bitter, green shards slicing my throat as I tried to swallow them.

facts.fact: 她甩开那念头，去摸手里的线：两个结——两场考验已过，还剩两场
facts.anchor: I shook the thought from my head and fingered the thread in my hand instead. Two knots. Two challenges down. Two more to go.

facts.fact: 她曾把这边的房子想象成一个整洁的隐修处、一个嬉皮派对屋、一座奢华的女神神庙；真看到时却有点"雷声大雨点小"
facts.anchor: After all the different ways I’d imagined this side of the house—a tidy hermitage, a hipster party pad, a luxurious temple to the feminine divine—seeing it for real was anti-climactic somehow.

facts.fact: 就像你当面质问出轨的恋人、对方却哭起来：你不太能生出同情，但也不再那么理直气壮地愤怒了
facts.anchor: Like when a cheating lover cries when you confront them and you can’t quite feel pity for them but you’re not as righteously angry anymore.

facts.fact: 这一次没有音乐，也没有诱人的光和暖把她引向下一层
facts.anchor: This time there was no music, no inviting light and warmth drawing me to the next level.

facts.fact: 脚下的楼梯变软了，地毯更厚、也更磨破
facts.anchor: The stairs became soft underfoot. The carpet grew thicker and more frayed.

facts.fact: 她意识到自己不是在往下走，而是在一个阴沉的下午走上一座长草的山坡
facts.anchor: I realised I was no longer descending, but walking up a grassy hill on an overcast afternoon.

facts.fact: 忽然，她闻到了海
facts.anchor: And then suddenly, I could smell the sea.

facts.fact: 山坡平缓下来，她站在海滩上方、靠近她长大的那座镇子的悬崖上
facts.anchor: The hill levelled off and I was on the cliffs above the beach close to the town where I’d grown up.

facts.fact: 某人的格子围巾被风卷着飞过崖边
facts.anchor: Someone’s tartan scarf went flying over the cliff edge.

facts.fact: 她父亲裹着抓绒衣和防水外套，抓紧一小卷细线，把自己稳在草地上
facts.anchor: My father, wrapped in a fleece and a waterproof, was anchoring himself into the grass as he gripped a fine spool of string.

facts.fact: 两个小姑娘——最漂亮的卷发、甜心的脸蛋、完美的一对——靠在她父亲腿边，笑着接过风筝线：Grayson 家的女孩
facts.anchor: Two little girls, with the prettiest curls and sweetheart faces, a perfect pair, leaned into my father’s legs, giggling and smiling as he passed them the kite string. The Grayson girls.

facts.fact: 路过的老夫妇赞许地微笑："如今这年头，看到一个男人拥抱父职是好事。"
facts.anchor: “This day and age, it’s good to see a man embrace fatherhood.”

facts.fact: 可那两个笑着的快乐女孩，都不是她父亲的女儿
facts.anchor: Except neither of the smiling, happy girls were my father’s daughter.

facts.fact: 母亲对她说的版本不同："她们没有父亲了，让她们跟你爸玩吧。分享是好事。"
facts.anchor: They don’t have a father anymore, she’d said, so let them play with your dad. It’s good to share.

facts.fact: 可她也开始拔自己的头发、咬掉嘴唇上的皮
facts.anchor: But I also started pulling out my hair and biting the skin off my lips.

facts.fact: 学校里她趁 Lucy 要坐下时把椅子抽走
facts.anchor: I pulled the chair out from under her as she went to sit down.

facts.fact: 父亲先到走廊去看 Lucy，蹲下来擦她的眼泪、抱了她，然后一言不发地给她办了离校手续、开车带她回家
facts.anchor: He checked on Lucy first out in the hallway. He got down on her level and wiped away her tears and gave her a hug.

facts.fact: 她记得自己想象灵魂离开身体、飞上山崖上空灰色的天，像一只黄色风筝，明亮又自由
facts.anchor: I remember imagining I’d left my body and was flying up into a grey sky over the cliffs, a yellow kite, brilliant and free.

facts.fact: 她这才注意到风筝线是红色的——一卷红线
facts.anchor: I noticed now that the kite string was red. A spool of red string.

facts.fact: 父亲啧了一声："Tammy，这什么话。"
facts.anchor: “Such language, Tammy.” My father tutted.

facts.fact: 父亲对她说："看她们多会分享？你真该对她们好一点。你根本不知道她们过得多难。"
facts.anchor: “See how well they share?” my father said to me. “You really should have been better to them. You’ve no idea how hard it’s been for them.”

facts.fact: 她爆发：她们的父亲没死、没抛下她们，甚至没离开这座镇子，只是搬到了两条街外
facts.anchor: Their father didn’t die. He didn’t leave them. Fuck, he didn’t even leave the town. He moved two streets over.

facts.fact: 她说：Laura-Ann 美甲课毕业时，你给她买了车
facts.anchor: When she”—I pointed at Laura-Ann, the smallest girl—“graduated from her nail course, you got her a car.

facts.fact: 而她大学毕业时，只得到一顿"去找工作"的说教
facts.anchor: But when I graduated from uni, I just got a lecture on finding a job.

facts.fact: "那你们他妈离婚的时候，谁在我身边？"
facts.anchor: “Then who was there for me when you got fucking divorced?”

facts.fact: 母亲不在了——她搬到南方，改嫁进一个大家族
facts.anchor: My mother was gone. She moved down south and remarried into a large family.

facts.fact: 父亲点头叹气："我想你现在够大了，可以知道真相了。"
facts.anchor: “I suppose you’re old enough now to know the truth.”
